questions.question: When approaching a curve during the driving test, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Slow down before entering the curve.
Keep your vehicle in its lane.
Use the brakes steadily throughout the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brakes steadily throughout the curve.
questions.explanation: When approaching a curve, check traffic in all directions. Slow down before entering the curve so you do not need to brake or shift gears while turning. Stay in your lane and keep checking traffic. Do not brake while turning.

questions.question: Driving at night is:

options.text: Safer than driving during the day.
Just as safe as driving during the day.
More dangerous than driving during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous than driving during the day.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous. You cannot see hazards as well. Headlight glare can reduce your vision. More tired and impaired drivers are on the road at night.

questions.question: Pressing and releasing the brake pedal too many times can:

options.text: Release air faster than the compressor can replace it.
Add more air to the braking system.
Make the brake pedal more sensitive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release air faster than the compressor can replace it.
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, pressing and releasing the brake pedal too many times removes air faster than the compressor can put it back.

questions.question: On long trips, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Take rest breaks.
questions.explanation: Take a break every 100 miles or every 2 hours to avoid fatigue. Driving at night or when you would normally be sleeping increases the risk of accidents caused by tiredness.

questions.question: Black ice is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Usually thin.
questions.explanation: Black ice is thin and clear. You can see the road through it. It looks like a wet road. Watch for black ice when the road looks wet but the temperature is below freezing.

questions.question: To avoid a hazard, you:

options.text: Should always come to a complete stop.
May need to swerve out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: May need to swerve out of the way.
questions.explanation: Stopping is not always possible. If you cannot stop in time to avoid a hazard, swerving may be your safest choice.

questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use ____ air brake systems.
questions.correctAnswerText: Dual
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems.

questions.question: You may:

options.text: Have more than one license if one is for business purposes.
Have more than one license if they are from different states.
Not have more than one license.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not have more than one license.
questions.explanation: You cannot have more than one driver license at a time. States share information to prevent this. Breaking this law can result in fines or jail time.

questions.question: When backing with a trailer, you should start by:

options.text: Turning the steering wheel toward the direction you want to go.
Turning the steering wheel away from the direction you want to go.
Turning the wheel as sharply as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning the steering wheel away from the direction you want to go.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, turn the steering wheel away from the direction you want to go. Once the trailer starts to turn, turn the wheel the opposite way to follow the trailer.

questions.question: People working on a disabled vehicle:

options.text: May be focused on repairs and not watching traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be focused on repairs and not watching traffic.
questions.explanation: Be careful when driving near people working on a disabled vehicle on the roadside. They are focused on the repair and may not notice nearby traffic.

questions.question: When should you turn off your turn signal?
questions.correctAnswerText: After you finish the turn
questions.explanation: Keep your signal on during the entire turn. Turn it off only when the turn is complete.

questions.question: Blocking is used to:

options.text: Keep cargo in a large box
Stop cargo from sliding in a trailer
Stop cargo from falling out of a trailer

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop cargo from sliding in a trailer
questions.explanation: Blocking is placed on all sides of cargo to keep it from sliding when the vehicle moves.

questions.question: Is emergency equipment required in a vehicle?

options.text: Only for vehicles carrying hazardous materials

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is required
questions.explanation: Check for emergency equipment during pre-trip inspection. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and one charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: What must happen before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes?

options.text: The brakes maintain full air pressure when the engine is off
The brakes maintain some air pressure when the engine is off
The engine must run to build enough air pressure for the brakes to work
No time is needed to build air pressure before driving

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine must run to build enough air pressure for the brakes to work
questions.explanation: Before driving, run the engine to let the air compressor build at least 100 psi of air pressure in both the primary and secondary brake systems.

questions.question: What happens to your speed when driving downhill?

options.text: You will come to a complete stop

questions.correctAnswerText: Your speed increases
questions.explanation: Gravity pulls your vehicle down a slope, causing your speed to increase.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, what happens when air pressure is lost and spring brakes activate?

options.text: A separate air tank can release the spring brakes for a short time
You can continue driving normally with the spring brakes
The air tanks automatically refill to a safe pressure level

questions.correctAnswerText: A separate air tank can release the spring brakes for a short time
questions.explanation: A separate air tank can temporarily release the spring brakes if they activate due to low air pressure. This allows the driver to move the vehicle in an emergency.

questions.question: What may be included in a basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: Driving straight into a parking space

questions.correctAnswerText: Parallel parking
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test includes straight line backing, offset parking, parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: To show other drivers that you are angry
To warn other drivers that you are nearby

questions.correctAnswerText: To warn other drivers that you are nearby
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn others of your presence. Use it only when necessary because it can startle other drivers.

questions.question: What makes up the emergency brake system?

options.text: Only parts of the parking brake system
Only parts of the service brake system
Parts of both the parking and service brake systems

questions.correctAnswerText: Parts of both the parking and service brake systems
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three separate braking systems: service brakes, parking brakes, and emergency brakes. The emergency brake system uses parts from both the parking and service brake systems.

questions.question: What should a driver ensure about the truck?

options.text: Most of the cargo is in the front of the trailer

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck is properly loaded
questions.explanation: Proper cargo loading is essential for safe truck operation. Improper loading affects how the vehicle handles and can damage it. Cargo that is not secured properly can fall and cause injury or death.

questions.question: When are most drivers the least alert?
questions.correctAnswerText: At night
questions.explanation: Most drivers are least alert at night. Tiredness and lack of focus are major dangers when driving at night, especially after midnight.

questions.question: When checking the exhaust system, which defects should be fixed?

options.text: A broken exhaust pipe, muffler, or tailpipe

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Exhaust system problems are serious because poisonous fumes can enter the vehicle. Before a trip, check for loose, broken, or missing pipes, mufflers, tailpipes, brackets, clamps, bolts, or nuts. Also check that exhaust parts are not rubbing against tires or fuel system parts, and that nothing is leaking.

questions.question: Brake linings should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Free of oil
questions.explanation: Brake linings should not be loose. They should not be wet with oil or grease. They should also not be too thin.

questions.question: If you meet an aggressive driver, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Ignore their gestures
questions.explanation: Do not react to angry gestures from other drivers. Avoid looking at them and do not try to race them.

questions.question: Hydroplaning:

options.text: Only happens at very high speeds
Can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph
Happens most when tire pressure is too high
Happens most when tires have good tread

questions.correctAnswerText: Can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water on the road. It is most likely when tire pressure is too low or when tread is worn.

questions.question: If an air compressor belt is belt-driven, it should be checked to make sure it is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Properly tightened
questions.explanation: If your vehicle has air brakes, check the air compressor belt before each trip. Make sure the belt is tight and in good condition.

questions.question: After the engine starts, warning lights and buzzers should:

options.text: Turn off once the vehicle moves

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off right away
questions.explanation: Warning lights and buzzers should turn off immediately after the engine starts. This includes the charging circuit, oil, coolant, and Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) warning lights.

questions.question: In hot weather, spots on the road where tar is bleeding are:

options.text: As grippy as the rest of the road
More grippy than the rest of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Very slippery
questions.explanation: In hot weather, tar in the road rises to the surface. These spots are very slippery, so watch out for them.

questions.question: What are placards?

options.text: Signs on a vehicle that show what hazardous cargo is inside
A type of tire for snowy roads

questions.correctAnswerText: Signs on a vehicle that show what hazardous cargo is inside
questions.explanation: Placards are diamond-shaped warning signs placed on vehicles carrying hazardous materials. They identify the type of hazard in the cargo.

questions.question: Before a trip, you should check that:

options.text: The pedal grooves have not worn smooth

questions.correctAnswerText: The pedal grooves have not worn smooth
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip check, make sure nothing blocks the pedals. Check that all pedals work properly and that their grooved surfaces are not worn smooth.

questions.question: When can brakes get out of adjustment?
questions.correctAnswerText: If they get too hot.
questions.explanation: Brakes can go out of adjustment quickly if they overheat from heavy use. Check your brakes often.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, what will you be asked to do?

options.text: Explain what you inspect and why.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain what you inspect and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must do a complete inspection. You must explain to the examiner what you are inspecting and why.

questions.question: Why should you do pre-trip inspection steps in the same order every time?

options.text: You will be less likely to skip a step.
The form must be followed in order.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be less likely to skip a step.
questions.explanation: Using the same routine every time helps you remember all the steps. A regular pattern makes it less likely you will forget something.

questions.question: When stopping, how should you press the brake pedal?
questions.correctAnswerText: Press down slowly and smoothly.
questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal down slowly and smoothly. Control the pressure to bring your vehicle to a safe stop.

questions.question: Why must you drain air tanks regularly?

options.text: Because air becomes old and needs replacing.
Because compressed air contains water that must be removed.
To remove bad air from the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains water that must be removed.
questions.explanation: Compressed air in brake systems contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up. Drain the tanks regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: If one-fourth of the leaves are missing from a leaf spring during inspection, what should happen?

options.text: The driver can drive at reduced speeds.
The vehicle must be taken out of service for repairs.
The vehicle is safe to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle must be taken out of service for repairs.
questions.explanation: Missing or broken leaves in a leaf spring are dangerous. If one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing, the vehicle must stop being used until it is fixed.

questions.question: What comes out when you drain an air tank?
questions.correctAnswerText: Water and oil.
questions.explanation: Air tanks have drains that remove water and compressor oil. Letting these build up can damage the brakes.

questions.question: What can happen if you do not drain air brake tanks?

options.text: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.
questions.explanation: Air brake tanks must be drained to remove water and oil. If not drained, water buildup can freeze in cold weather and cause brake failure.

questions.question: When checking the fifth wheel during inspection, what should you look for?

options.text: The locking jaws should be open.
The locking jaws should be closed tight around the kingpin.
The locking jaws should be loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: The locking jaws should be closed tight around the kingpin.
questions.explanation: Check that the fifth wheel locking jaws are closed around the kingpin shaft, not around the kingpin head.

questions.question: How far ahead should you look while driving?
questions.correctAnswerText: 12 to 15 seconds.
questions.explanation: Look at least 12 to 15 seconds ahead of your vehicle. This helps you spot hazards early and react safely. Watch for vehicles entering the highway or changing lanes.

questions.question: How do you test the low pressure warning signal?

options.text: Turn on the engine and apply the trailer hand brake.
Press and release the brake pedal quickly several times.
Remove wheel chocks and disengage the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and release the brake pedal quickly several times.
questions.explanation: Your low pressure warning light must work properly. After the system charges, test it by pressing and releasing the brake pedal quickly. This releases air from the brake system. The warning signal should turn on when pressure drops to a dangerous level.

questions.question: When checking a power steering system, what should you look for?

options.text: The fluid is at the correct level.
The hoses are connected to the battery.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fluid is at the correct level.
questions.explanation: Check the power steering hoses, pumps, and fluid level. Look for and repair any leaks before driving the vehicle.

questions.question: What is true about a fatigued driver?

options.text: They should take over-the-counter pills to stay awake.
They may make critical decisions too slowly.
They are usually more careful than other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may make critical decisions too slowly.
questions.explanation: When fatigued, you will not see or react to hazards as quickly. You will be slower at making important decisions.

questions.question: How do you release the parking brake?

options.text: Tap the brake pedal three times.
Push in the brake control knob.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push in the brake control knob.
questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, a yellow diamond-shaped knob controls the parking brakes. Pull the knob out to set the parking brakes. Push it in to release them.

questions.question: What happens to a vehicle's speed when going downhill?
questions.correctAnswerText: It increases.
questions.explanation: Gravity pulls the vehicle faster when traveling downhill, so speed will increase.

questions.question: What should you do with power steering hoses?
questions.correctAnswerText: Check them for leaks.
questions.explanation: When checking a power steering system, inspect the hoses, pumps, and fluid level. Make sure the hoses are not leaking.

questions.question: What is true about a distracted driver?

options.text: They usually react well to hazards.
They are usually aware of what is happening around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: They usually notice things slower.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving causes slower awareness, delayed decisions, and wrong actions. Watch for distracted drivers and avoid them when possible.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Let the rear wheels lock up.
Tell other drivers you are braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents the wheels from locking when you brake hard on a slippery surface.

questions.question: Why should flares be used carefully after an accident?

options.text: Spilled fuel on the ground could catch fire.
Other drivers may not see them in sunny weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spilled fuel on the ground could catch fire.
questions.explanation: Spilled fuel can catch fire if flares are used nearby. Use flares carefully after an accident.

questions.question: When you start an engine, how long should it take for oil pressure to reach normal?
questions.correctAnswerText: Within seconds.
questions.explanation: Check your gauges when you start the engine. Oil pressure should reach normal within a few seconds.
